fixed.reason: Residual under strict PTX, in both builds. The fix inserts __syncthreads() at fixed :760, between each thread's __threadfence() (:750) and thread 0's atomicInc (:764). Every warp's L322 atomics are now barrier-ordered before block A's signal. That closes the gap the commit describes (lagging warps still issuing atomicAdds when thread 0 signals), so the hardware-observable failure is gone. It does not give PTX happens-before from A's L322 atomics to B's reads. (1) Reader side, unchanged by the fix: in B, thread 0's atomicInc (:764) is a relaxed RMW with no fence after it. B's own __threadfence (:750) comes before it, and __syncthreads_or (:767) is CTA scope only. So B has no acquire pattern, and A's release (fence; atomicInc) does not synchronize with B. (2) Writer side: a lagging thread t's fence sits before the barrier. It is not in program order before thread 0's atomicInc, and thread 0's own fence also comes before the barrier, so thread t's atomic is not in the causal past of the fence of thread 0's release pattern. The pairs of the buggy build therefore stay unordered in the fixed build: L322 vs L361 (SC), L322 vs L382/L383 (DR), and the extra_pairs L322 vs L366 (SC) and L322 vs the reset (DR; :776 buggy, :786 fixed). A detector that follows PTX should report them in both builds. It reports them in the buggy build only if it treats the per-thread fence + barrier + relaxed atomicInc + __syncthreads_or idiom as release/acquire, which over-approximates PTX (compare T12's instance gate: acq needs CCTL.IVALL after the RMW, and there is none here). CLAUDE.md T21 item 3 already lists raft-1 as a possible fixed-build residual.

Fixed build: whether the evaluated detector models the last-block idiom (fence, barrier, relaxed ATOMG.E.INC by thread 0, __syncthreads_or, then plain/volatile reads by the last block) as ordering. The reader side has no acquire fence after the atomicInc in either version; a strict-PTX detector would then report the same pairs in the fixed build too (residual in both versions, not caused by the bug). 'absent' follows verify.expected_report_fixed (writer side fixed).

The driver uses IdxT=int64_t and dense layout; the upstream flaky test (issue 2997) is SelectKCsrTest_float_int (csr layout, int index). The racy code (L321-L323, L361, L382-L383, L750-L769) is layout-independent but the SASS widths (.64 here) would be .32 for IdxT=int.

review.notes: Buggy sites confirmed at 32df870: atomicAdd(histogram + i, histogram_smem[i]) at :322 in the merge loop :321-:323, after the :318 barrier, executed by threads i < num_buckets. __threadfence() at :750 by every thread, then thread 0's atomicInc at :753-:756 with no barrier in between, then __syncthreads_or at :757. The last block runs scan(volatile IdxT*) at :767 (8-bit: num_buckets 256 < BlockSize 512, so the else branch: volatile load :361 and store :366; 11-bit: BlockLoad :349 / BlockStore :355), choose_bucket at :769 (plain loads :382/:383) and the reset at :776. The bug (A's lagging warp still at :322 when A's thread 0 signals) gives the oracle's pairs: atomic vs volatile = SC, atomic vs plain = DR, so expected_class DR+SC is right. The class follows from the access strengths (T10/D9, D12). D20 decides only how the SC pair counts: under D20 (i) both pairs score in their classes, under (ii) only the DR pair. Hence depends_on_D20 = true. class_reason's '(D20)' tag on the DR pair should be read that way. Thread relation (cross-block, with the missing intra-block ordering cross-warp) confirmed. A's accesses before the :318 barrier (out_buf/out writes, filter_cnt/out_cnt atomics, the kth_value_bits read :265) are barrier-ordered before A's fence. With no acquire in B they are, under strict PTX, unordered in both builds against B's choose_bucket write of counter->kth_value_bits (:391), the :783 filter_cnt reset and the fused last_filter reads. Those are not the bug and are not listed as pairs; triage any such report as the reader-side idiom.
